title: 547. The French Revolution: The Execution of the King (Part 4)

sentences.en: Frenchman, where now are those qualities which once distinguished you?
sentences.zh: 法国人，那些曾经让你们引以为傲的品质现在在哪里？

sentences.en: Where now is that national character of greatness and loyalty?
sentences.zh: 伟大与忠诚的民族性格现在在哪里？

sentences.en: Would you show your powers in overwhelming with misfortunes the man who had the noble resolution to repose such confidence in you?
sentences.zh: 难道你们要以惨痛的不幸来压倒那个曾对你们抱有如此信任、展现出高尚决心的男人，以此来显耀你们的力量吗？

sentences.en: Have you no more respect for the sacred duties of hospitality?
sentences.zh: 难道你们对神圣的待客之道已不再有一丝敬意？

sentences.en: Is no commiseration due to such unparalleled misfortunes?
sentences.zh: 难道如此空前的不幸不该得到一丝同情吗？

sentences.en: Do you not think that a king who ceases to be one is not a victim sufficiently striking without its being necessary to add such accumulated miseries to his fate?
sentences.zh: 难道你们不认为，一个不再是国王的国王已经是一个足够震撼的牺牲品，无需再将如此深重的苦难强加于他的命运吗？

sentences.en: Frenchman, this revolution which regenerates you develops great qualities.
sentences.zh: 法国人，这场使你们重生的革命激发了伟大的品质。

sentences.en: But fear, lest it should at the same time efface humanity from your heart without which every other virtue is loSt.
sentences.zh: 但你们要当心，莫让它同时也抹去了你们心中的人性，失去了人性，其他一切美德都将不复存在。

sentences.en: So that was the somewhat florid concluding statement of a fellow called Romain de Cez, who was a lawyer from Bordeaux.
sentences.zh: 那是波尔多律师罗曼·德·塞兹一段相当华丽的结辩陈词。

sentences.en: Tom writes here that he was celebrated for his sonorous eloquence.
sentences.zh: 汤姆在这里写道，他以声如洪钟的雄辩力而闻名。

sentences.en: As I think you can tell.
sentences.zh: 我想你们也能听出来。

sentences.en: As you can tell, there he was standing on the 26th of December 1792 before the National Convention in Paris.
sentences.zh: 如你们所见，在1792年12月26日那天，他正站在巴黎的国民公会前。

sentences.en: And of course, the man he was defending, who was on trial for his life, was the erstwhile King Louis XVI.
sentences.zh: 当然，他所辩护的那个人——正面临生死审判的——正是曾经的国王路易十六。

sentences.en: And this, Tom, is one of those speeches that defines the French Revolution.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这就是定义了法国革命的那些演讲之一。

sentences.en: The French Revolution is a great rhetorical event.
sentences.zh: 法国大革命是一场伟大的修辞事件。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And we've done a lot of great orations.
sentences.zh: 我们已经做过很多伟大的演讲了。

sentences.en: We had Saint-Just last time saying that you can't reign innocently and the king must die.
sentences.zh: 上一次我们提到圣茹斯特说，你不可能无罪地统治，国王必须死。

sentences.en: And here we have Romain de Cez saying that you should fear lest you efface humanity from your heart.
sentences.zh: 而在这里，我们有罗曼·德·塞兹说，你们应该心存敬畏，免得抹去了内心的同情。

sentences.en: And you should find the compassion for this man who has suffered enough.
sentences.zh: 你们应该对这个已经遭受够了苦难的人心生怜悯。

sentences.en: And basically, nobody listens.
sentences.zh: 而基本上，根本没人听。

sentences.en: Well, I think some people do listen, as we will see.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为还是有人听的，正如我们将会看到的。

sentences.en: But they, from Louis' point of view, don't listen hard enough, I think you could say.
sentences.zh: 但站在路易的角度来看，他们听得还不够认真，我想你可以这么说。

sentences.en: And that translation that you read, it was issued, published only a few weeks after it was delivered.
sentences.zh: 你所朗读的那段翻译，是在它发表后仅仅几周内就印行出版的。

sentences.en: So it was rushed translated into English.
sentences.zh: 所以它是被仓促翻译成英文的。

sentences.en: And I guess it's a reminder of just how seismic an event the trial of the King of France is.
sentences.zh: 我想这也提醒了我们，审判法国国王是一件多么震撼的事件。

sentences.en: I mean, it completely transfixes France, obviously, but Britain, all of Europe.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它显然彻底震动了法国，还有英国以及整个欧洲。

sentences.en: I mean, it's the most astonishing spectacle.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是最令人震惊的奇观。

sentences.en: And in Britain and in the other monarchies of Europe, public opinion, by and large, is appalled.
sentences.zh: 在英国和欧洲的其他君主国，公众舆论总体上感到震惊。

sentences.en: Even though, obviously, in England, the English had actually set a precedent because they had tried and executed a king themselves in the form of Charles I.
sentences.zh: 尽管显而易见的是，在英国，英国人其实已经开过先例了，因为他们曾以查理一世的形式亲自审判并处决过一位国王。

sentences.en: Not uncontroversial, right?
sentences.zh: 并非毫无争议，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But it's not just in foreign monarchies that public opinion is appalled, because there are also deep reservoirs of royalism in France.
sentences.zh: 但感到震惊的不仅是外国君主国的公众舆论，因为在法国也有着深厚的保王主义基础。

sentences.en: And the assumption that a king is inviolate, down to the most basic level, that people shouldn't touch him without kind of strict protections of ritual and so on.
sentences.zh: 那种认为国王不可侵犯的观念，在最根本的层面上，即人们不应该在没有严格的礼仪保护等情况下去触碰他。

sentences.en: This is deeply, deeply ingrained.
sentences.zh: 这是根深蒂固的。

sentences.en: It's been a theme of French history for a millennium and more.
sentences.zh: 这千百年来一直是法国历史的一个主题。

sentences.en: And that sense that a king's actions are inviolate,
sentences.zh: 那种认为国王的行为不可侵犯的意识，

sentences.en: it had been so hardwired that it had been written into the constitution that had been issued in 1791 and which Louis had accepted.
sentences.zh: 已经根深蒂固到被写进了1791年颁布并被路易所接受的宪法中。

sentences.en: And in that, it had specified that only if a king had set himself at the head of a hostile army could he be reckoned to have abdicated the throne.
sentences.zh: 其中明确规定，只有当国王把自己置于敌对军队的统帅地位时，方可被视为退位。

sentences.en: But otherwise, and this is something that Louis himself points out at his trial, the king's person is inviolable and sacred.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外——这也是路易在审判时亲自指出的——国王的人身是不可侵犯且神圣的。

sentences.en: That is what the constitution had said.
sentences.zh: 宪法就是这么说的。

sentences.en: But we've been talking about this second revolution that has overwhelmed Paris and France over the course of 1792.
sentences.zh: 但我们一直在谈论这第二场革命，它在1792年席卷了巴黎和法国。

sentences.en: And it is precisely that sense of inviolability, precisely the sense that the king's very body is somehow sacred, that the deputies in the national convention are, you know,
sentences.zh: 正是那种不可侵犯感，正是那种认为国王的躯体本身某种程度上是神圣的观念，国民公会中的代表们，你们知道，

sentences.en: that is what they're trying to destroy.
sentences.zh: 那正是他们试图摧毁的东西。

sentences.en: They're not just trying to destroy the person of Louis, they're trying to destroy the figure of the king and everything, all the sacrality that is associated with him.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅在试图摧毁路易这个人，他们还在试图摧毁国王这个形象以及一切与他相关的神圣性。

sentences.en: And that's why they're bringing him to trial.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们为什么要对进行他审判的原因。

sentences.en: That's the whole point of it.
sentences.zh: 这才是整件事情的关键所在。

sentences.en: And of course, they know that the eyes of the world upon them.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们也知道全世界的目光都聚焦在他们身上。

sentences.en: The international situation for this is incredibly important.
sentences.zh: 这背后的国际形势极其重要。

sentences.en: We were talking yesterday about these amazing successes that French arms have been having, going into Switzerland and into Nice and into the Austrian Netherlands,
sentences.zh: 我们昨天还在讨论法军取得的那些惊人胜利，他们开进瑞士、尼斯和奥属尼德兰，

sentences.en: what's now Belgium.
sentences.zh: 也就是现在的比利时。

sentences.en: And the justification for this is precisely the overthrow, not just of tyranny and monarchy in France, but across Europe, across the world.
sentences.zh: 这样做的正当理由恰恰是为了推翻暴政和君主制，不仅在法国，还要在全欧洲、全世界。

sentences.en: I mean, we were saying that the French revolutionary leaders are seeing what they're doing in cosmic terMs.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们当时说过，法国革命领袖们是以宏大的历史眼光来看待他们的所作所为的。

sentences.en: It's kind of Trotskyite in that sense, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这有点像托洛茨基主义，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's interesting how that has escalated from an opposition to this king, which would have been the case a year earlier,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，这种对抗是如何从一年前原本只是针对这位国王的反对意见升级而来的，

sentences.en: that this king is complicit with counter-revolutionaries and foreign infiltrators and all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 即这位国王与反革命分子和外国潜入者串通一气之类的事情。

sentences.en: But it has widened, hasn't it?
sentences.zh: 但它的范围扩大了，不是吗？

sentences.en: They've self-radicalised.
sentences.zh: 他们实现了自我激进化。

sentences.en: So now it is in opposition to all kings and to kingship more generally.
sentences.zh: 因此，现在的反对对象已经变成了所有的国王以及更广泛的君主制。

sentences.en: And so this has become more than just a case about Louis and his own personal misdemeanors.
sentences.zh: 所以这已经不仅仅是一起关于路易及其个人过失的案件了。

sentences.en: He is on trial as a symbol of worldwide despotism and monarchy.
sentences.zh: 他作为世界范围内的专制和君主制的象征正受审。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it's monarchy.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是君主制。

sentences.en: It's the very concept of monarchy itself.
sentences.zh: 这就是君主制这个概念本身。

sentences.en: So one of the deputies who's pushing for the guilty verdict on the king says that the verdict that is delivered on Louis must serve as an example for all nations.
sentences.zh: 因此，一位推动对国王做出有罪判决的代表表示，对路易做出的判决必须成为所有国家的榜样。

sentences.en: So this is very pointed.
sentences.zh: 所以这是非常明确的指向。

sentences.en: If it's Louis XVI today, then perhaps it will be George III in a court in London tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 如果今天审判的是路易十六，那么明天或许就会是在伦敦法庭上审判乔治三世。

sentences.en: That's a horrendous thought, Tom.
sentences.zh: 这是一个可怕的想法，汤姆。

sentences.en: Well, OK.
sentences.zh: 好吧，行。

sentences.en: So we shouldn't exaggerate how focused on other countries the delegates are.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不应该夸大代表们对其他国家的关注程度。

sentences.en: I mean, they are.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们的确关注。

sentences.en: But of course, their real focus is on France itself.
sentences.zh: 但当然，他们真正的焦点还是法国本土。

sentences.en: And again, we talked yesterday how it's important for the new republic because there hasn't been a formal proclamation of a republic.
sentences.zh: 同样，我们昨天讨论过这对于新共和国有多么重要，因为当时还没有对共和国进行正式的公告。

sentences.en: So just to quote Antoine de Becq.
sentences.zh: 这里就引用一下安托万·德·贝克的话吧。

sentences.en: Dominic, do you want to insert your joke there?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你想在那里插个笑话吗？

sentences.en: He was later on Strictly Come Dancing.
sentences.zh: 他后来上了《舞动奇迹》。

sentences.en: That's the joke.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个笑话。

sentences.en: Very good.
sentences.zh: 非常好。

sentences.en: So he wrote this great book, Glory and Terror, Seven Deaths Under the French Revolution.
sentences.zh: 所以他写了这本出色的书，《荣耀与恐怖：法国大革命下的七次死亡》。

sentences.en: And the Princesse de Lambelle is one of those seven deaths, but Louis XVI is another.
sentences.zh: 朗巴勒亲王夫人是那七次死亡之一，而路易十六则是另一个。

sentences.en: And he writes, when France entered into a republic in the course of the summer of 1792, it did not solemnly proclaim the foundation of a new regime.
sentences.zh: 他写道，当法国在1792年夏天的进程中进入共和国时，它并没有庄严宣告一个新政权的建立。

sentences.en: The historian can look.
sentences.zh: 历史学家可以去寻找。

sentences.en: Nowhere will he unearth an official decree in the archives installing the first French republic.
sentences.zh: 他绝不会在档案馆里翻出任何确立法兰西第一共和国的官方法令。

sentences.en: So you do have the image of liberty on the melted royal seal.
sentences.zh: 所以你确实在融化的王室印章上看到了自由的形象。

sentences.en: We talked about that.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论过那个。

sentences.en: But otherwise, there isn't really anything kind of symbolically resonant.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，并没有真正具有某种象征共鸣的东西。

sentences.en: And I guess that that is what Saint-Just had fixed on in his famous speech when you quoted him yesterday.
sentences.zh: 我想这正是圣茹斯特在他昨天的名言中紧紧抓住的一点。

sentences.en: That the king, simply by virtue of being a king, is guilty, since Saint-Just puts it.
sentences.zh: 正如圣茹斯特所言，国王仅仅因为身为国王就是有罪的。

sentences.en: One cannot reign innocently.
sentences.zh: 一个人不可能无罪地统治。

sentences.en: And so it's only when the king has been put to death that the republic can properly be born.
sentences.zh: 因此，只有当国王被处死后，共和国才能真正诞生。

sentences.en: So in the Marseillais, there's talk about tainted blood fertilizing the soil.
sentences.zh: 所以在《马赛曲》中，有关于用污浊的血来滋润土地的说法。

sentences.en: And I'm sure that that must be kind of part of what the deputies are thinking.
sentences.zh: 我确信这一定也是代表们脑海中想法的一部分。

sentences.en: They want a big set piece.
sentences.zh: 他们想要一场大型的重头戏。

sentences.en: Yeah, but his blood will fertilize the soil and enable the republic to kind of flourish and grow and emerge.
sentences.zh: 是的，但他的血将滋润土地，使共和国得以蓬勃发展、壮大并崛起。

sentences.en: And there's a sense in which, therefore, I think the deposition, the imprisonment, the trial, and perhaps if he's found guilty,
sentences.zh: 因此从某种意义上说，我认为废黜、监禁、审判，以及如果他被判有罪的话，

sentences.en: the execution of the king will serve the French republic as all the various declarations in the American Revolution served the American republic.
sentences.zh: 对国王的处决，将为法兰西共和国起到美国革命中所有各种宣言对美利坚共和国所起的作用。

sentences.en: It's the ritualistic kind of kickoff, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这是一种充满仪式感的开端，对吧？

sentences.en: And you say if he's found guilty, there is no doubt that he will be found guilty from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 你刚才说“如果他被判有罪”，毫无疑问他从一开始就会被判有罪的。

sentences.en: I mean, we're going to be talking about the trial, but I don't think there's any doubt in anybody's mind that he's not going to be walking out a free man,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们接下来会谈到这场审判，但我认为所有人心里都很清楚，他绝不可能大摇大摆地以一个自由人的身份走出去，

sentences.en: kind of punching the air and stuff outside the old bailey.
sentences.zh: 在老贝利法院外面振臂高呼之类的。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: No, I just wanted to maintain the suspense.
sentences.zh: 不，我只是想保持悬念。

sentences.en: Yeah, okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧，行。

sentences.en: It's all about the jeopardy.
sentences.zh: 这全是为了制造危机感。

sentences.en: Okay, very good.
sentences.zh: 好的，非常好。

sentences.en: Dramatic tension.
sentences.zh: 戏剧性的张力。

sentences.en: So tell us exactly how he is brought to trial.
sentences.zh: 那么请给我们讲讲他是具体如何被送上审判台的。

sentences.en: Okay, so on the 10th of December, the formal indictment is read out in the National Convention,
sentences.zh: 好的，在12月10日，正式的起诉书在国民公会上被宣读，

sentences.en: and Louis is charged with conspiring with the enemies of the French nation against the republic and of, therefore, of direct treason.
sentences.zh: 路易被指控与法国人民的敌人勾结以对抗共和国，因此犯有直接叛国罪。

sentences.en: And essentially what they do is they go back over everything that he's done since the outbreak of the revolution in 1789, and they present it in the worst light possible.
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，他们回顾了他在1789年革命爆发以来所做的一切，并以最恶劣的光景呈现出来。

sentences.en: And if you're a royalist, you might say, well, this is very harsh.
sentences.zh: 如果你是个保王党，你可能会说，这太严厉了。

sentences.en: Personally, I think actually they've got Louis pretty bang to rights because he has been working to undo the revolution.
sentences.zh: 就我个人而言，我认为他们实际上已经把路易抓了个现行，因为他一直在致力于瓦解革命。

sentences.en: And the thing is, is that the worst thing that he's been doing, which is essentially, you know, he has been conspiring with the Austrians.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，他做过最恶劣的事情，基本上就是，你知道的，他一直在与奥地利人勾结。

sentences.en: He has been writing to monarchs of hostile nations.
sentences.zh: 他一直在给敌对国家的君主写信。

sentences.en: That correspondence has not come to light, even when the safe was opened.
sentences.zh: 那些信件并没有大白于天下，哪怕在保险箱被打开时也是如此。

sentences.en: That evidence of that had gone because Louis and Marie Antoinette had been sensible enough to actually burn that.
sentences.zh: 这方面的证据已经消失了，因为路易和玛丽·安托瓦内特足够明智，把那些信件都烧掉了。

sentences.en: So they don't even know the worst of it.
sentences.zh: 所以他们甚至不知道最糟糕的情况。

sentences.en: So, as you say, I think the evidence is pretty bad that he has been betraying the revolution.
sentences.zh: 因此，正如你所说，我认为有证据表明他背叛了革命，情况相当糟糕。

sentences.en: So the following day on the 11th of December, he is summoned to the convention to face the charges that are going to be leveled against him.
sentences.zh: 所以在接下来的12月11日，他被传唤到公会去面对将要指向他的指控。

sentences.en: And the summons is brought to him by the mayor of Paris.
sentences.zh: 传唤令是由巴黎市长亲自带给他的。

sentences.en: He, of course, is in the temple where he's been locked up for about four months.
sentences.zh: 他当然是在圣殿塔里，在那里他被关了大约四个月。

sentences.en: The mayor comes into his presence, doesn't take his hat off, doesn't bow, addresses him as Louis Capet.
sentences.zh: 市长来到他面前，没有脱帽，没有鞠躬，直呼他为路易·卡佩。

sentences.en: And we talked about that yesterday, that Capet is the family name of Hugh Capet, who had been elected king at the end of the 10th century.
sentences.zh: 我们昨天讨论过，卡佩是于格·卡佩的家族姓氏，他在10世纪末被选为国王。

sentences.en: And Louis is very indignant and points out that he is not a Capet, that he is a Bourbon,
sentences.zh: 路易对此非常愤慨，指出他不是卡佩，而是波旁，

sentences.en: because the Capets had gone extinct in the early 14th century, which is what had kicked off the Hundred Years' War.
sentences.zh: 因为卡佩家族在14世纪初就已经绝嗣了，这也是引发百年战争的导火索。

sentences.en: Or they'd been replaced by the Valois, and then the Valois had gone extinct and they'd been replaced by the Bourbon.
sentences.zh: 或者说他们被瓦卢瓦家族取代了，然后瓦卢瓦家族也绝嗣了，接着他们被波旁家族取代了。

sentences.en: And so, why Capet?
sentences.zh: 所以，为什么要叫卡佩？

sentences.en: The reason is precisely because it enables the Republic to demonstrate that it's not just Louis who's on trial,
sentences.zh: 原因恰恰在于，这使得共和国能够表明，受审的不仅仅是路易个人，

sentences.en: it's the entire line of all the kings that join Hugh Capet to Louis XVI.
sentences.zh: 而是将于格·卡佩与路易十六连接起来的所有历代国王的整个世系。

sentences.en: So the trial is doing two things simultaneously, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这场审判同时在做两件事，对吧？

sentences.en: It's trying Louis as a private individual who has betrayed the revolution.
sentences.zh: 它既在审判路易作为背叛革命的个人，

sentences.en: But it's also doing that Saint-Just thing, of trying him as a symbol of monarchy.
sentences.zh: 但它同时也在践行圣茹斯特的那套做法，将他作为君主制的象征来审判。

sentences.en: He stands in, effectively, for all the monarchs that France has ever had.
sentences.zh: 实际上，他代表了法兰西曾经拥有过的所有君主。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think there's an inherent ambivalence there, because on the one hand, the emphasis is on his role now as someone who has been de-crowned, who is just a normal citizen.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为其中存在一种内在的矛盾，因为一方面，重点在于他现在作为被废黜者的角色，他只是一个普通公民。

sentences.en: But of course, he isn't.
sentences.zh: 但当然，他并不是。

sentences.en: He has to be tried as a king as well.
sentences.zh: 他也必须作为一名国王来接受审判。

sentences.en: So there's a kind of slight ambivalence there that shadows the entire approach of the Republic to Louis and to his fate.
sentences.zh: 因此，有一种轻微的矛盾情绪笼罩着共和国对待路易及其命运的整个方针。

sentences.en: So he leaves the temple, as we said, for the first time in about four months.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，他离开了圣殿塔，这是大约四个月来的第一次。

sentences.en: A massive lines of soldiers along the streets of the National Guard to make sure that no rescue attempts can be made.
sentences.zh: 国民自卫军在国民公会的街道两旁列队，人数众多，以确保不会发生任何营救企图。

sentences.en: He is brought into the convention.
sentences.zh: 他被带进了国民公会。

sentences.en: He's led to the bar.
sentences.zh: 他被带到了审判栏前。

sentences.en: He is obviously dressed as a private citizen.
sentences.zh: 他显然穿着普通公民的衣服。

sentences.en: An onlooker describes him as wearing just a plain yellowish frock coat.
sentences.zh: 一位旁观者形容他穿着一件朴素的 yellowish（微黄色）短大衣。

sentences.en: He walks in.
sentences.zh: 他走了进来。

sentences.en: He looks around.
sentences.zh: 他环顾四周。

sentences.en: Everyone is sat.
sentences.zh: 所有人都坐着。

sentences.en: Everyone has their hats on.
sentences.zh: 所有人都戴着帽子。

sentences.en: And onlookers are delighted by his expression of kind of consternation, really.
sentences.zh: 旁观者们对他的那种惊愕的表情感到非常高兴。

sentences.en: And so one of them wrote,
sentences.zh: 其中一个人写道：

sentences.en: no doubt he was quite surprised to see no other seat for him than a humble chair in a place where he had more than once deployed all the pride and ceremony of royalty.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，当他发现自己在一个曾多次展现王室骄傲与礼仪的地方，除了一个简陋的椅子之外竟然没有别的座位时，他感到十分惊讶。

sentences.en: Remember, readers, the scarlet armchair with fleur-de-lis, which insulted the representatives of the nation.
sentences.zh: 记住，读者们，那个绣着金百合花的红色靠背椅，正是它侮辱了国家代表。

sentences.en: And of course, he is only allowed to sit when he is given permission to do so by the president of the court.
sentences.zh: 当然，只有在得到法庭庭长的准许后，他才被允许坐下。

sentences.en: And this is to turn the world upside down.
sentences.zh: 这简直是要把世界颠倒过来。

sentences.en: You think of all the ritual that had governed behavior at Versailles.
sentences.zh: 你想想凡尔赛宫里那些规范行为的繁文缛节。

sentences.en: And it's utterly upended, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 而这一切全都被彻底颠覆了，不是吗？

sentences.en: This is very execution of Charles I, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这简直就是查理一世受审的重演，不是吗？

sentences.en: We did two episodes about that with our friend Ted Valance.
sentences.zh: 我们曾和我们的朋友特德·瓦兰斯一起做过两期关于这个的节目。

sentences.en: Remember, there's all that business where a bit of Charles' cane falls off and no one picks it up.
sentences.zh: 记得吗，有那么一段插曲，查理的藤条掉了一截，结果没人去捡。

sentences.en: Yeah, and he has to get it.
sentences.zh: 对，然后他只好自己去拿。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: This is all exactly the same thing again.
sentences.zh: 这完全又是同一回事。

sentences.en: And obviously, they all know the story of Charles I, so there must be a slight element of role-playing on all sides, actually.
sentences.zh: 显然，他们都知道查理一世的故事，所以各方其实都带有一点角色扮演的成分。

sentences.en: That they're kind of conscious that this has happened before.
sentences.zh: 他们心里清楚，这种事以前发生过。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And as we will see, Louis is very familiar with the story of Charles' trial.
sentences.zh: 正如我们将看到的，路易对查理受审的故事非常熟悉。

sentences.en: And it's probably that that enables it, you know, having read that, having read how Charles maintained his dignity in that situation.
sentences.zh: 正是这一点成全了他，你知道的，读过这些之后，读过查理在那种情况下如何保持尊严之后。

sentences.en: I'm sure it must steal Louis in this situation, because when the charges are read out, he is very calm in denying them.
sentences.zh: 我确信这一定给了路易在当前局势下的底气，因为当宣读指控时，他非常平静地予以否认。

sentences.en: People say, even those who are hostile to him, say he seems very serene.
sentences.zh: 人们说，即使是那些对立的人也说，他看起来非常安详。

sentences.en: And even when, you know, he's shown these papers with his signature on that have been taken from the safe, that, you know, he's clearly banged to rights.
sentences.zh: 甚至当人们向他展示那些从保险箱里搜出来的、签有他名字的文件时，那些明显证据确凿的东西。

sentences.en: And he just said, that's not my signature.
sentences.zh: 他只是说，那不是我的签名。

sentences.en: It's nothing to do with me at all.
sentences.zh: 这跟我一点关系都没有。

sentences.en: And the only time he actually displays any sense of outrage or indignation is when he's accused of shedding French blood.
sentences.zh: 他唯一一次表现出某种愤慨或气愤，是当他被指控流淌了法国人的鲜血时。

sentences.en: And then he, you know, he is indignant.
sentences.zh: 然后他，你知道的，他感到愤慨。

sentences.en: He protests.
sentences.zh: 他抗议。

sentences.en: He says, this is absolutely false.
sentences.zh: 他说，这完全是捏造。

sentences.en: And the reaction to his performance, the Montagnat, so the radicals, Robespierre, Marat, and so on, they view this as the rankest hypocrisy that he is blatantly lying.
sentences.zh: 而山岳派——也就是激进派罗伯斯庇尔、马拉等人——对他的表现的反应是，认为这是最无耻的虚伪，他是在公然说谎。

sentences.en: A majority of people in the convention, though, I think they feel sufficiently sympathetic that they decide that Louis should be allowed legal representation,
sentences.zh: 不过，国民公会中的大多数人似乎抱有足够的同情心，他们决定应该允许路易拥有法律辩护权，

sentences.en: because that had not been decided until this point.
sentences.zh: 因为直到这一点之前，这都还没决定呢。

sentences.en: So, Louis is taken back to the temple, and he is then allowed to request legal representation.
sentences.zh: 于是，路易被带回圣殿塔，随后他被允许请求法律辩护。

sentences.en: And so the person he goes for is the guy who probably has the most formidable reputation of any of the lawyers who had been operating in the Auxian regime.
sentences.zh: 因此，他选中这个人，大概是旧制度下所有活跃的律师中名声最显赫的一个。

sentences.en: And this is the guy who had led the defense of the Prince de Rouen in the affair of the diamond necklace.
sentences.zh: 就是那个在钻石项链案中领导鲁昂王子辩护的人。

sentences.en: The cardinal guy.
sentences.zh: 那个红衣主教的人。

sentences.en: The cardinal.
sentences.zh: 那个红衣主教。

sentences.en: The cardinal de Rouen, who, by successfully defending the cardinal de Rouen, had done terrible damage to Marie Antoinette and to Louis XVI himself, to the very image of the crown.
sentences.zh: 鲁昂红衣主教，他通过成功为鲁昂红衣主教辩护，对玛丽·安托瓦内特和路易十六本人，对王室的整体形象造成了可怕的打击。

sentences.en: That seems a long time ago now, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 现在看来，那已经是好久以前的事了，不是吗？

sentences.en: The diamond necklace affair.
sentences.zh: 钻石项链案。

sentences.en: And it must have done to Louis himself, because even though this guy, who's a man called Guijon Baptiste, had inflicted these wounds on the monarchy, in the revolution itself,
sentences.zh: 对路易本人来说肯定也是如此，因为尽管这家伙——一个名叫纪尧姆·巴蒂斯特的人——曾在革命中对君主制造成过这些创伤，

sentences.en: he had been a very enthusiastic supporter of constitutional monarchy.
sentences.zh: 但他曾是君主立宪制非常热情的支持者。

sentences.en: So he'd been a member of the Third Estate, but had been a kind of constitutional monarchiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以他曾是第三等级的成员，但属于那种立宪保皇派。

sentences.en: And he'd stuck to that.
sentences.zh: 而且他一直坚持这一点。

sentences.en: And he was the guy who'd come up with the idea that Louis should no longer be king of France, but should be king of the French.
sentences.zh: 他就是那个提出以下想法的人：路易不应再是法兰西国王，而应是法国人的国王。

sentences.en: That's very much where he's at.
sentences.zh: 这很符合他的立场。

sentences.en: But because of that, of course, he now seems a counter-revolutionary.
sentences.zh: 但也正因如此，他现在看起来成了一个反革命分子。

sentences.en: The guy who had been at the cutting edge of radicalism in 1788 now seems total reactionary.
sentences.zh: 这个曾在1788年处于激进主义最前沿的人，现在看起来彻底成了一个反动派。

sentences.en: And he's aware of this.
sentences.zh: 他自己也意识到了这一点。

sentences.en: And so he says he's not going to do it.
sentences.zh: 所以他说他不会接这个活。

sentences.en: But there's also an issue.
sentences.zh: 但这里还有一个问题。

sentences.en: He's got an issue, to be fair to him, with his weight, hasn't he?
sentences.zh: 说句公道话，他体重大得有问题，不是吗？

sentences.en: He says, basically, I'm too fat to stand up in court.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是说，我太胖了，在法庭上站不住。

sentences.en: That's his excuse.
sentences.zh: 这就是他的借口。

sentences.en: So this had been royalist abuse levelled at him right the way back in the trial of the Cardinal Trojan, that he'd simply been too fat even to stand up.
sentences.zh: 早在审判特洛伊红衣主教时，保皇党就曾以此嘲讽过他，说他胖得甚至连站都站不稳。

sentences.en: But now he takes advantage of this, says, I can't possibly, you know, I'll just keel over if I have to stand up all this time.
sentences.zh: 但现在他利用了这一点，说我绝对不行，你知道的，如果我得一直站着，我就会直接晕倒。

sentences.en: So that's his excuse.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是他的借口。

sentences.en: Now, fortunately for Louis, there are people who are brave enough to volunteer for the job of defending him.
sentences.zh: 现在，对路易来说幸运的是，有一些人勇敢到自愿承担为他辩护的工作。

sentences.en: And one of them is our friend, Olympe de Gouges, the feminiSt.
sentences.zh: 其中一位就是我们的朋友、女权主义者奥兰普·德古热。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So she has not been keeping her head out of the firing line.
sentences.zh: 所以她一直没有避开风头。

sentences.en: She has been publicly attacking Robespierre, attacking Marat.
sentences.zh: 她一直在公开攻击罗伯斯庇尔，攻击马拉。

sentences.en: She's very identified with the Girondins, who she sees as being much more sympathetic to female suffrage.
sentences.zh: 她与吉伦特派紧密相连，在她看来吉伦特派对女性选举权要同情得多。

sentences.en: And people may remember that she was very, very fond of Louis.
sentences.zh: 人们可能还记得，她非常非常喜欢路易。

sentences.en: She viewed him as having been dealt a bad hand.
sentences.zh: 在她看来，路易只是拿到了一手烂牌。

sentences.en: And even as the king is being brought to trial, she issues a public statement declaring that the greatest of Louis' crimes is to have been king at a time in philosophy,
sentences.zh: 甚至在国王正面临审判时，她也发表了一份公开声明，宣称路易最大的罪过，就是在那个时代的哲学中成为了一名国王，

sentences.en: was silently preparing the foundations of our republic.
sentences.zh: 而哲学当时正在默默地为我们的共和国奠定基础。

sentences.en: We have abolished royalty.
sentences.zh: 我们已经废除了君主制。

sentences.en: He has lost his subjects, his throne, everything.
sentences.zh: 他失去了臣民、王位以及一切。

sentences.en: Let us be good enough to leave him his life.
sentences.zh: 让我们发发善心，留下他的性命吧。

sentences.en: And I think in saying that, she's probably speaking for a sizable number of the French who probably do feel that.
sentences.zh: 我想她这么说，大概也是代表了相当一部分法国人的心声，他们可能确实是这么想的。

sentences.en: I mean, you could say she might be being naive, because by leaving him alive, you would create problems for the future.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以说她可能太天真了，因为留下他的性命会为未来埋下隐患。

sentences.en: But, you know, she's being commendably compassionate, Tom.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，她表现出了值得称赞的同情心，汤姆。

sentences.en: Well, this is not how the Saint-Culot see it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，无套裤汉可不这么看。

sentences.en: So they are furious at this.
sentences.zh: 所以他们对此愤怒至极。

sentences.en: And a large mob gathers outside her house with the bravery that is absolutely typical of her.
sentences.zh: 一大群暴民聚集在她家门外，而她展现出了完全符合其性格的勇敢。

sentences.en: Olympe de Gouges goes down and confronts them on her doorstep.
sentences.zh: 奥兰普·德古热走下楼去，在自家门廊前与他们对质。

sentences.en: And one of the Saint-Culot grabs her by her hair, you know, holding up her face to the crowd and says, you know, let's chop this off.
sentences.zh: 其中一个无套裤汉抓住她的头发，你知道的，把她的脸抬起来对着人群说，你知道的，让我们把这颗脑袋砍下来吧。

sentences.en: I'm going to auction it off.
sentences.zh: 我要把它拿去拍卖。

sentences.en: Who bids for her head?
sentences.zh: 谁出价买她的头？

sentences.en: And Olympe de Gouges puts in a massive bid.
sentences.zh: 而奥兰普·德古热竟然出了个极高的竞标价。

sentences.en: And this is treated by the crowd as, you know, immense banter.
sentences.zh: 这被人群当作了一种巨大的玩笑，你知道的。

sentences.en: Hilarious.
sentences.zh: 太搞笑了。

sentences.en: And so they let her off.
sentences.zh: 于是他们放了她一马。

sentences.en: So her good humour, her ability to make a joke in the teeth of mob violence enables her to fight another day.
sentences.zh: 因此，她的好幽默，她在面对暴民暴力时开玩笑的能力，让她得以绝处逢生。

sentences.en: But Louis doesn't fancy her as his legal representative.
sentences.zh: 但路易并不看好她来做自己的法律辩护人。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: I mean, it would have been amazing if he had.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果他真选了那才叫惊奇呢。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: He is not sufficiently progressive to do that.
sentences.zh: 他的思想还没进步到那个地步。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Fortunately, there is another guy who volunteers, and this is a man called Guillaume Chrétien de Malzerbe.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，还有另一个人志愿加入，这人名叫纪尧姆·克雷蒂安·德马尔泽尔布。
zh_words: 纪尧姆·克雷蒂安·德马尔泽尔布

sentences.en: And he is the absolute embodiment of kind of enlightenment-infused liberalism.
sentences.zh: 他简直就是那种充满启蒙精神的自由主义的化身。

sentences.en: So he's a friend.
sentences.zh: 所以他是位朋友。

sentences.en: He was a friend of Rousseau.
sentences.zh: 他曾是卢梭的朋友。

sentences.en: He corresponded with Diderot.
sentences.zh: 他与狄德罗有书信往来。

sentences.en: He'd been the censor, the national censor under Louis.
sentences.zh: 他曾在路易手下担任审查官，即国家审查官。

sentences.en: And he'd allowed Diderot to publish the encyclopedia, which was kind of very radical, very atheist-tinged, very keen botaniSt.
sentences.zh: 他曾允许狄德罗出版《百科全书》，那本书相当激进，带有强烈的无神论色彩，而他本人是个狂热的植物爱好者。

sentences.en: And again, he is a bit like Baptiste.
sentences.zh: 同样，他有点像巴蒂斯特。

sentences.en: He's an example of how the whirly gig of politics is leaving one-time radicals behind and casting them as reactionaries.
sentences.zh: 他是一个生动的例子，说明政治的风云变幻是如何将昔日的激进派抛在身后，并将他们打入反动派行列的。

sentences.en: But he, unlike Baptiste, is prepared to come out and defend the king.
sentences.zh: 但他与巴蒂斯特不同，他准备挺身而出为国王辩护。

sentences.en: So he's actually retired.
sentences.zh: 所以他其实已经退休了。

sentences.en: He's 71.
sentences.zh: 他71岁了。

sentences.en: He's kind of very elderly.
sentences.zh: 他非常年迈了。

sentences.en: And he's the one who recruits Romain de Céz, the orotund guy who likes the sound of his own voice.
sentences.zh: 正是他招募了罗曼·德塞兹，那个声音洪亮、喜欢听自己说话的律师。

sentences.en: There's also another distinguished lawyer called François Tanchet.
sentences.zh: 此外还有另一位杰出的律师叫弗朗索瓦·坦谢。

sentences.en: So the three of them are appointed to defend the king.
sentences.zh: 于是他们三人被指派为国王辩护。

sentences.en: And they have two weeks to prepare their case.
sentences.zh: 他们有两个星期的时间来准备辩护词。

sentences.en: And so they go to the cell in the temple where Louis is now being kept in isolation.
sentences.zh: 于是他们前往圣殿塔的牢房，路易目前正被单独关押在那里。

sentences.en: So he's been separated from his family.
sentences.zh: 因此他与家人隔绝了。

sentences.en: And they start preparing their defense.
sentences.zh: 他们开始着手准备辩护。

sentences.en: And it was with Malzerbe that in 1788, Louis had discussed the trial of Charles I.
sentences.zh: 正是在1788年，路易曾与马尔泽尔布讨论过查理一世的审判问题。

sentences.en: Oh, in 1788.
Yeah, interesting.
sentences.zh: 对，有意思。

sentences.en: There are foundations there.
sentences.zh: 这其中是有历史渊源的。

sentences.en: And of course, what Charles I's strategy in his trial had been to refuse to accept the legitimacy of the court.
sentences.zh: 当然，查理一世在审判中的策略一直是拒绝承认法庭的合法性。

sentences.en: I mean, obviously, he had his head cut off, but he was always going to.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，显然他的头还是被砍了，但无论如何他都难逃一死。

sentences.en: But historians would generally say that that was very clever from Charles, because actually he was right.
sentences.zh: 不过历史学家通常会说，查理这一招非常聪明，因为他其实是对的。

sentences.en: The court was illegitimate.
sentences.zh: 那个法庭本就是非法的。

sentences.en: And he basically said, come on, everyone knows this is a put-up job and has no legal foundation.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是说，得了吧，大家都知道这是一场内定戏，没有任何法律依据。

sentences.en: And he wasn't wrong.
sentences.zh: 而且他说得没错。

sentences.en: And he got a lot of sympathy for that.
sentences.zh: 他也因此赢得了许多同情。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And Malzerbe, who's a very smart lawyer, very familiar with his English history, this is the strategy that he wants Louis to adopt.
sentences.zh: 而马尔泽尔布作为一名极其精明的律师，对英国历史又了如指掌，这正是他希望路易采取的策略。

sentences.en: To insist on the wording of the original written constitution, which says that the king is inviolable.
sentences.zh: 坚持最初成文宪法的字面表述，即宪法规定国王是不容侵犯的。

sentences.en: Which in turn would be to attack the entire legitimacy of this second revolution that's happened over the course of 1792.
sentences.zh: 进而以此来全面攻击1792年以来发生的这场第二次革命的合法性。

sentences.en: And this is exactly what the Montagnard had been afraid that they would do.
sentences.zh: 而这正是山岳派一直以来最害怕他们会做的事。

sentences.en: The trial would become, it wouldn't just be a trial of Louis, it would be a trial of the new constitutional settlement.
sentences.zh: 审判将不再仅仅是对路易的审判，而会变成对新的立宪体制的审判。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So throughout this history, we have discussed how whenever Louis is given an option, he always chooses the dumb option.
sentences.zh: 所以在整段历史中我们已经讨论过，每当路易面临选择时，他总是会选那个愚蠢的选项。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And this is what he does again.
sentences.zh: 而这一次他又这么做了。

sentences.en: He turns down Malzerbe's advice.
sentences.zh: 他拒绝了马尔泽尔布的建议。

sentences.en: He says, no, I'm going to answer all these points that had been raised against him,
sentences.zh: 他说，不，我要逐一反驳所有针对他的指控，

sentences.en: all the disparagements of his motivations and actions over the course of the previous years since the fall of the Bastille.
sentences.zh: 反驳自巴士底狱陷落以来几年间，对他动机和行动的所有诋毁。

sentences.en: He's obviously personally indignant about this and he wants to take them down.
sentences.zh: 他对此显然感到个人尊严受到触犯，并且想要逐一反驳。

sentences.en: But of course, it's madness because he has no prospect of convincing the court.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这简直是疯了，因为他根本没有任何希望说服法庭。

sentences.en: He has no prospect of making a proper case.
sentences.zh: 他没有任何可能做出一场像样的辩护。

sentences.en: Malzerbe's strategy is the only effective one, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为马尔泽尔布的策略才是唯一有效的方案。

sentences.en: I suppose there are two interesting things there.
sentences.zh: 我想这里有两点很有意思。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So number one is, the weird thing is that answering point by point, it is madness because on some of those points, he is clearly guilty.
sentences.zh: 所以第一点是，奇怪的是，逐点反驳简直是疯了，因为在其中某些指控上，他显然是罪证确凿的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He did flight to Varennes.
sentences.zh: 他确实出逃过瓦雷讷。

sentences.en: He did get in touch with the Austrians.
sentences.zh: 他确实与奥地利人接触过。

sentences.en: He has been in touch with counter-revolutionaries.
sentences.zh: 他一直在与反革命分子保持联系。

sentences.en: He has been conspiring against the revolution.
sentences.zh: 他一直在密谋反对革命。

sentences.en: But the interesting thing is that in his own mind, clearly, Louis doesn't think he's guilty.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，在路易自己的心中，他显然不认为自己有罪。

sentences.en: He thinks these guys are bad people who have done a coup and have seized control of the revolution.
sentences.zh: 他认为这些人是一群坏蛋，发动了政变并夺取了对革命的控制权。

sentences.en: Actually, I am blameless.
sentences.zh: 实际上，我是无可指责的。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the interesting thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是最有趣的地方。

sentences.en: He wouldn't choose that strategy if he didn't have absolute confidence in his own innocence.
sentences.zh: 如果他对自己的清白没有绝对的信心，他是绝不会选择这种策略的。

sentences.en: And I think that's what explains his serenity.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是他表现得如此安详的原因所在。

sentences.en: Absolute conviction that he's completely in the right.
sentences.zh: 坚信自己完全正确。

sentences.en: Kind of a slight Prince Andrew quality, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 或许有点安德鲁王子的气质。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: You know, just madness.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，简直就是疯狂。

sentences.en: Anyway, he's the king.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，他才是国王。

sentences.en: And so, well, he's not the king anymore, but as far as Malzerb is concerned, he is.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，他不再是国王了，但在马尔泽布看来，他依然是。

sentences.en: So that's the strategy that they have to adopt.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是他们必须采取的策略。

sentences.en: So, again, this is very Cromwellian.
sentences.zh: 所以，同样地，这非常具有克伦威尔色彩。

sentences.en: The date for the trial is set on the 26th of December.
sentences.zh: 审判日期定在12月26日。

sentences.en: So the day after Christmas.
sentences.zh: 也就是圣诞节的第二天。

sentences.en: So there's a kind of deliberate attempt to ignore the sacral quality of the feast day.
sentences.zh: 因此，这是一种刻意无视这个节日神圣属性的尝试。

sentences.en: So on Christmas Day itself, Louis dictates his will to Malzerb, suggesting that he knows what's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 所以在圣诞节当天，路易向马尔泽布口述了他的遗嘱，暗示他已经知道将要发生什么。

sentences.en: And then the following day, he's duly brought back to the convention.
sentences.zh: 然后在第二天，他按时被带回国民公会。

sentences.en: And the trial happens.
sentences.zh: 审判随即开始。

sentences.en: And this is when Desaes gives his famous speech.
sentences.zh: 这就是德塞发表其著名演讲的时候。

sentences.en: And you ask, does it persuade anyone of Louis' innocence?
sentences.zh: 你会问，这说服了任何人相信路易是无辜的吗？

sentences.en: Probably not.
sentences.zh: 大概没有。

sentences.en: But does it persuade anyone that he should be spared execution?
sentences.zh: 但它说服了任何人认为他应该免于死刑吗？

sentences.en: Well, maybe it does.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也许有吧。

sentences.en: Because the convention are going to vote on whether Louis is guilty.
sentences.zh: 因为国民公会将就路易是否有罪进行投票。

sentences.en: And as you say, that's pretty much guaranteed he will be found guilty.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，他被判定有罪几乎是板上钉钉的。

sentences.en: But then they have to decide on a verdict.
sentences.zh: 但随后他们必须对判决做出决定。

sentences.en: And in fact, they end up voting on a third point of principle.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们最终对第三个原则问题进行了投票。

sentences.en: Because the Girondins, at the end of December, who clearly feel that the execution of the king will be seen as a kind of Montagnard triumph.
sentences.zh: 因为吉伦特派在12月底时，显然觉得国王被处决会被视为一种山岳派的胜利。

sentences.en: They want to stop that happening.
sentences.zh: 他们想阻止这种情况发生。

sentences.en: They propose that the verdict that the convention arrives at should be put to a referendum.
sentences.zh: 他们提议将国民公会达成的判决提交给全民公投。

sentences.en: And this also has the additional benefit of enabling them to pose as the defenders of popular sovereignty.
sentences.zh: 这还有一个额外的好处，就是能让他们以人民主权的捍卫者自居。

sentences.en: But in the long run, very bad move for the Girondins in this.
sentences.zh: 但从长远来看，这对吉伦特派来说是一个非常糟糕的举动。

sentences.en: I mean, and one of their own goals that they have been scoring for the last few months, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就像他们过去几个月里一直在自摆乌龙，对吧？

sentences.en: That they keep coming up with these wheezes that don't quite work.
sentences.zh: 他们总是想出这些不太管用的歪点子。

sentences.en: And which make them look royaliSt.
sentences.zh: 这让他们看起来像保王党。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the madness.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是疯狂之处。

sentences.en: None of them are royaliSt.
sentences.zh: 他们当中没有人是保王党。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，一点没错。

sentences.en: So the Montagnard, you know, they're very indignant at this.
sentences.zh: 所以山岳派对此感到非常愤怒。

sentences.en: They regard it as terrible.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这太糟糕了。

sentences.en: And out on the streets of Paris, the Saint-Culot also are appalled by the idea that Louis' fate should be protracted.
sentences.zh: 在巴黎街头，无套裤汉也对拖延路易命运的想法感到震惊。

sentences.en: So on the 30th of December, delegates from about 18 of the sections in Paris, so these are the kind of the local councils in Paris,
sentences.zh: 所以在12月30日，来自巴黎约18个区（也就是巴黎的类似地方委员会）的代表，

sentences.en: petition the convention for the tyrant to be put to death immediately.
sentences.zh: 向国民公会请愿，要求立即处死这个暴君。

sentences.en: And it's full melodrama.
sentences.zh: 这简直是一场彻头彻尾的苦情戏。

sentences.en: They've got women who are carrying the bloody clothes of relatives who died on that day.
sentences.zh: 他们带着那天死去的亲属的血衣的妇女。

sentences.en: They've got people who are kind of hobbling in on crutches after they'd been shot or stabbed in the leg by the Swiss guards.
sentences.zh: 还有一些人，在被瑞士卫兵开枪击中或刺伤腿后，一瘸一拐地拄着拐杖走进来。

sentences.en: But it's all absolutely calculated to tug at the heartstrings of upstanding patriots.
sentences.zh: 但这完全是经过精心计算的，旨在触动正直爱国者们的心弦。

sentences.en: And then just when it seems that things can't get any worse for the Girondins, there's another bombshell.
sentences.zh: 就在吉伦特派似乎已经走投无路的时候，又一枚重磅炸弹落下了。

sentences.en: Because early in January, letters are produced showing that three of them, three leading Girondins,
sentences.zh: 因为在一月初，有信件被出示，显示他们当中的三人、三位主要的吉伦特派成员，

sentences.en: had been corresponding with the king in the days building up to the massacre on the 10th of August, the attack on the Tuileries.
sentences.zh: 在8月10日大屠杀和攻击杜伊勒里宫之前的几天里，曾与国王有书信往来。

sentences.en: Because at that point, some of them are hoping he might bring them back into his ministry and that they wouldn't have to have this kind of coup.
sentences.zh: 因为当时他们中的一些人希望国王能让他们重返内阁，这样他们就不必经历这种政变了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And their claim is, which I'm sure is absolutely genuine, is that they'd been communicating with the king because they were anxious to save the fatherland.
sentences.zh: 他们的说法——我确信绝对是真实的——是他们与国王通信是因为他们急于拯救祖国。

sentences.en: Because this was the period when the Prussians were advancing and everything seemed in a state of disaster.
sentences.zh: 因为那是普鲁士军队推进、一切似乎都处于灾难状态的时期。

sentences.en: But obviously, this brands them at the very least as lacking in confidence in the martial prowess of the patriotic armies.
sentences.zh: 但显然，这给他们打上了对爱国军队的尚武精神缺乏信心的烙印。

sentences.en: So that's a bad look.
sentences.zh: 所以这相貌极不光彩。

sentences.en: And of course,
sentences.zh: 当然，

sentences.en: it's particularly bad because you mentioned in the previous episode that the correspondence between the king and queen and Mirabeau had been produced from the king's safe.
sentences.zh: 情况之所以格外糟糕，是因为你在上一集里提到过，国王和王后与米拉波之间的信件是从国王的保险箱里搜出来的。

sentences.en: And so this sense that everywhere you look, there is treason and treachery and the mask of patriotism is hiding rankist treason.
sentences.zh: 所以这种感觉是，无论你望向哪里，都有叛国和背叛，爱国主义的面具下隐藏着极度可耻的叛国行径。

sentences.en: This, again, is terrible for the Girondins.
sentences.zh: 这对吉伦特派来说，又是一场灾难。

sentences.en: And it makes them seem like kind of closet royalists.
sentences.zh: 这让他们看起来像是隐蔽的保王党。

sentences.en: So very good news for the Montagnards.
sentences.zh: 所以这对山岳派来说是个好消息。

sentences.en: So all of which means that on the 15th of January, the convention is ready to have these three votes.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切意味着，在1月15日，国民公会准备进行这三次投票。

sentences.en: Is he guilty?
sentences.zh: 他有罪吗？

sentences.en: Should the verdict go to a referendum?
sentences.zh: 判决应该提交公投吗？

sentences.en: If he is guilty, what should the sentence be?
sentences.zh: 如果他有罪，刑罚应该是什么？

sentences.en: So the first motion, is Louis Capet guilty or not guilty?
sentences.zh: 所以第一个动议，路易·卡佩是有罪还是无罪？

sentences.en: Marat has introduced a motion which is passed that the vote should be public so that no traitors can practice behind kind of secrecy.
sentences.zh: 马拉提出了一项并已通过的动议，即投票必须公开，这样就没有叛徒可以在保密的幌子下搞鬼。

sentences.en: And surprise, surprise, a universal, absolute majority.
sentences.zh: 不出所料，全票绝对多数通过。

sentences.en: Nobody votes against the guilty verdict.
sentences.zh: 没有人投有罪判决的反对票。

sentences.en: Although there are 26 abstentions.
sentences.zh: 尽管有26人弃权。

sentences.en: There are 26 abstentions.
sentences.zh: 有26人弃权。

sentences.en: Yes, there are 26 abstentions.
sentences.zh: 是的，有26人弃权。

sentences.en: So he is duly found guilty.
sentences.zh: 所以他正式被判定有罪。

sentences.en: Then there's a vote on should it go to a referendum?
sentences.zh: 接下来是关于是否提交公投的投票。

sentences.en: And this is defeated 425 to 286.
sentences.zh: 结果以425票对286票被否决。

sentences.en: So that is a very embarrassing defeat for the Girondins.
sentences.zh: 这对吉伦特派来说是一次非常尴尬的失败。

sentences.en: And then there's the vote on what Louis' punishment should be.
sentences.zh: 接下来是关于路易的惩罚应该是什么的投票。

sentences.en: And this is an absolutely marathon session.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是一场马拉松式的会议。

sentences.en: It lasts for over 24 hours.
sentences.zh: 持续了24小时以上。

sentences.en: Every deputy has to go up to the tribunal, has to say what he thinks the verdict should be.
sentences.zh: 每个代表都必须走上法庭，说出他认为判决应该是什么。

sentences.en: They are allowed to explain why they have arrived at their decision.
sentences.zh: 他们被允许解释他们是如何做出决定的。

sentences.en: Some, you know, podcast style, duly go on for hours and hours.
sentences.zh: 有些人，你知道的，带着播客风格，滔滔不绝地讲了几个小时。

sentences.en: Others give slightly more concise summaries.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则给出了稍微更简明扼要的总结。

sentences.en: And various decisions are given.
sentences.zh: 并给出了各种判决。

sentences.en: So the obvious one is death.
sentences.zh: 显而易见的一个就是死刑。

sentences.en: The Montagnards are all over this.
sentences.zh: 山岳派对此举双手赞成。

sentences.en: You know, they think this is a great idea.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们认为这是个好主意。

sentences.en: So they're very keen.
sentences.zh: 所以他们非常热衷。

sentences.en: It is Robespierre, unsurprisingly, who gives the most ringing and kind of Roman explanation for it.
sentences.zh: 毫无意外，罗伯斯庇尔发表了最震撼人心且最具古罗马风格的解释。

sentences.en: I am inflexible in relation to impressors, he declares, because I am compassionate towards the oppressed.
sentences.zh: 他宣告：“对于压迫者我是冷酷无情的，因为我同情被压迫者。”

sentences.en: I do not recognise the humanity that butchers the people and pardons despots.
sentences.zh: “我不承认那种屠杀人民却宽恕专制君主的所谓人道。”

sentences.en: So this is how the man who had been very much against the death penalty justifies it.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个曾经坚决反对死刑的人是如何为之辩护的。

sentences.en: I vote for death because I'm so kind, is basically what he's saying.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是在说，我投死刑是因为我太善良了。

sentences.en: He's all about heart.
sentences.zh: 他满腔热血。

sentences.en: All heart.
sentences.zh: 全都是为了心慈手软。

sentences.en: And Dominic, the most startling person to vote for the death penalty?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，投票支持死刑最令人震惊的人是谁？

sentences.en: The worst man in this story.
sentences.zh: 这个故事里最坏的人。

sentences.en: Who's that?
sentences.zh: 那是谁？

sentences.en: This is Philippe Equality, who is the king's own cousin.
sentences.zh: 这就是路易-菲利普·平等，国王的亲表弟。

sentences.en: What a terrible man he is.
sentences.zh: 他真是一个可怕的人。

sentences.en: I mean, at least abstain or at least say exile or something like that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，至少弃权，或者至少说流放诸如此类的话。

sentences.en: But to go all in in this way for your own cousin, I think, is very, very bad behaviour.
sentences.zh: 但为了你自己的表弟这样全力以赴，我认为这是非常非常糟糕的行为。

sentences.en: Even death with a recommendation that the king be reprieved.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有人提出死刑并建议对国王予以缓刑。

sentences.en: Because that is what some people vote for.
sentences.zh: 因为那是某些人的投票选择。

sentences.en: So death and then a pardon.
sentences.zh: 所以是死刑加特赦。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Others vote for exile.
sentences.zh: 其他人则投票支持流放。

sentences.en: And this is generally proposed for geopolitical reasons, that the king should be kept as a hostage.
sentences.zh: 这通常是基于地缘政治原因提出的，即应该将国王作为人质扣留。

sentences.en: And then when peace terms have been negotiated with the kind of hostile powers, then perhaps he can be sent off into exile.
sentences.zh: 然后，当与敌对强权谈判达成和平条款后，或许可以把他流放出去。

sentences.en: There is a brilliant spin, a Rousseauist spin on this from Louis-Sébastien Mercier, the playwright who is a friend of Olymp de Gouges,
sentences.zh: 路易-塞巴斯蒂安·梅谢尔——这位曾是奥兰普·德古热朋友的剧作家，最终将成为反革命分子——对此提出了一个精彩的、卢梭式的脑洞，

sentences.en: who in the long run will become a counter-revolutionary.
sentences.zh: 不过他当时是国民公会的代表。

sentences.en: But he's a delegate in the convention.
sentences.zh: 他提议将王室成员流放到塔希提岛或南方的某个岛屿，

sentences.zh: 让他们在渔民小屋里回归自然、体验简朴生活，从而洗心革面。

sentences.en: so that contact with nature in the simplicity of a fishing hut would rehabilitate them.
sentences.zh: 人们会花大价钱看这个的。

sentences.en: People would pay good money for that.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个绝妙的主意。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a brilliant idea.
sentences.zh: 玛丽·安托瓦内特一定会喜欢这个的，对吧？

sentences.en: Marie Antoinette would love that, wouldn't she?
sentences.zh: 那是一场蜜月假期。

sentences.en: That's a honeymoon holiday.
sentences.zh: 是的，一个塔希提少女。

sentences.en: Yeah, a Tahitian maiden.
sentences.zh: 她可以像约瑟夫·班克斯那样钓鱼和冲浪。

sentences.en: She could do fishing and surfing like Joseph Banks.
sentences.zh: 那太棒了。

sentences.en: It would be great.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 梅谢尔是几位表示权衡利弊让他们感到身体不适的代表之一。

sentences.en: And Mercier is one of several delegates who say that he's found it very difficult weighing up the pros and cons has made him physically ill.
sentences.zh: 压力巨大。

sentences.en: Huge stress.
